questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The best ways to clean your home quickly and cheaply
Why women do more housework, and ways to share it
How washing machines changed family life
Why fathers want to work fewer hours each week
questions.why: Pippa says women often do most chores, and they'll hear about two projects helping couples share housework.

questions.q: How does Neil say chores are shared in his home?
options: His wife does almost everything
They pay someone to do the cleaning
He does all the cooking and she does the cleaning
Whoever isn't working at the time does the jobs
questions.why: His wife works part time and he works full time, so each does things when they're not working.

questions.q: What do figures from UN Women suggest?
options: Women do three more hours of unpaid work a day
Men now do more of the housework than women do
Women spend about three hours a week cleaning
Most families now share the housework equally
questions.why: The figures say women spend three hours more than men every day on unpaid care and domestic work.

questions.q: Why do household chores take a long time on the island of Rote?
options: Families there are very large, with many children
Women also have to work long hours in offices
There are few washing machines and no running water
The houses there are very big and hard to clean
questions.why: Neil says with few washing machines and no running water, domestic chores take a long time.

questions.q: Why does the reporter Ade Mardiyati mention that women on Rote also help in the fields?
options: To show that farming there is really quite easy work
To show the division of work isn't really fair
To explain why the men stay at home all day
To show that women prefer farming to housework
questions.why: She says you might think it's a fair division of labour, but women also help out in the fields.

questions.q: What does research suggest about women in wealthy countries?
options: They do less housework than women in traditional societies
They share housework equally with men
They mostly pay others to do chores
They also spend much more time than men on unpaid care work
questions.why: Neil says research suggests women in wealthy countries also spend much more time on unpaid care work.

questions.q: What does the Superdads project in Croatia do?
options: Pays fathers a monthly wage to stay at home
Teaches mothers how to relax after work
Runs workshops getting dads and sons to help
Trains men to become professional cleaners
questions.why: Anamarija Sočo leads workshops encouraging dads and sons to take some pressure off mums.

questions.q: According to Anamarija Sočo, how do mothers benefit when men do more chores?
options: They get more time for work, hobbies or rest
They earn more money in better-paid jobs
They no longer need to cook for the family
They can afford to move to a bigger house
questions.why: She says mothers have more space for their careers, hobbies or 'just simply to rest'.
